title: GATE 2027 Eligibility, Explained with Official Links
description: GATE 2027 eligibility: third year or higher of any undergraduate degree, or a completed one, and no age limit. The official criteria from IIT Madras in plain language, with eight common cases worked through.
author: Studyloaf Team

content.body: GATE's eligibility rules are broad, and they're easy to over-think. This post sets out the GATE 2027 criteria from the official website and information brochure, then applies them to common cases. The official eligibility page has the full degree-by-degree table, and it's the one that decides, so it's linked below.

content.heading: The criteria, in plain language
list: You're eligible if you're currently in the third year or higher of any undergraduate degree programme, or have completed any government-approved degree in engineering, technology, architecture, science, commerce, arts or humanities
M.B.B.S., B.D.S., B.V.Sc. and B.Sc. (Agriculture, Horticulture, Forestry) students are eligible from the 5th semester onwards, as are graduates of those degrees
With a degree from outside India, you need to be in the third year or higher of, or have completed, a bachelor's degree of at least three years in those fields

Certifications from professional societies (such as IE, ICE, IETE, AeSI, IIChE, IIM and IIIE) count only if they're approved by MoE, AICTE, UGC or UPSC as equivalent to B.E., B.Tech., B.Arch. or B.Planning
Candidates studying for or holding a higher degree than those in the eligibility table can also appear

content.heading: Eligibility is not admission
content.body: Being eligible to sit GATE says nothing about whether a particular programme will admit you. Each admitting institute sets and applies its own criteria for admission based on the GATE score, so read the notice of every programme you're aiming for, not just the GATE rules.

content.heading: Choosing a paper
content.body: GATE 2027 has 30 test papers, and you can sit one, or two from the official list of allowed combinations. Admission is decided by each admitting institute, so check which GATE papers a programme accepts in that programme's own notice before you choose.

content.heading: Common mistakes
list: Assuming a second-year student can apply early. The rule starts at the third year
Assuming GATE has an age limit. It doesn't
Treating eligibility for GATE as eligibility for a programme. Institutes decide admission
Relying on a summary (this one included) for an unusual degree. Check the full official table
